headlines.title: 24시간 외환시장 개방 에… 현물환 거래 10.1% 늘었다

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy shows mixed signals with improving exports and growth trajectories, but persistent headwinds in employment and inflation remain problematic. July job creation reached 108,000 persons year-over-year, yet unemployment rose to 2.6%, marking a 0.2 percentage point increase. Consumer price inflation moderated to 2.8% in July from 3.2% in June, but service sector inflation continued rising to 3.5%. The government emphasizes continued recovery momentum while acknowledging structural challenges in labor markets and rising household cost burdens.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government reported strengthened economic recovery momentum driven by export growth, with July employment figures showing expansion compared to prior year levels. However, the labor market faces increasing pressure with unemployment rising to 2.6% and employment rates declining to 63.3% year-over-year. Core inflation excluding food and energy prices increased to 2.6% from 2.5%, indicating persistent price pressures despite overall CPI moderation. Global economic conditions show steady growth, though risks from Middle East conflicts and U.S. tariff measures create uncertainty. The government acknowledges that while growth is strengthening, consumer livelihoods face continued strain from employment and inflation challenges.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSDAQ index rebounded 34% over two weeks to achieve the highest returns among major global stock indices this month, driven by regulatory relief for single-stock leveraged ETFs and reduced concentration in large semiconductor stocks. The KOSPI approached the 7000 level as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rebounded, though market participants remained cautious about sustainability. The upcoming FOMC meeting minutes on August 19 and various economic data releases next week will be critical in determining market direction. Growing retail investor participation across all demographics reflects shift from traditional savings products toward stock market investments, with ETF flows increasing significantly.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's battery industry is pivoting toward humanoid robotics as the next growth frontier, with all three major battery makers accelerating solid-state battery development. The global humanoid robot battery market is projected to expand dramatically from 1.4 billion dollars in 2035 to 10.5 billion dollars by 2040, with solid-state batteries expected to comprise over 50% of the market. LG's hardware capabilities in motors, sensors, batteries, and cooling systems are gaining renewed attention as AI integration becomes critical for robotics applications. However, the non-semiconductor sector faces structural headwinds, with electric vehicle production surging while traditional fuel vehicle markets decline sharply year-over-year.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's apartment market is undergoing significant structural transformation with accelerating shift from jeonse (long-term lease) to monthly rental arrangements, reflecting reduced affordability and changing housing demand patterns. Over 30,000 jeonse units have been converted to monthly rentals over seven years, while multi-child families and those relocating face unexpected tax penalties under new real estate policies. Government proposals to develop housing across the entire Yongsan Park area face implementation hurdles despite Ministry of Land, Infrastructure potential regulatory overrides. High-value apartment mortgage lending is facing stricter requirements next year, with regulatory changes incentivizing banks to prioritize mid-range housing loans. Rising interest in non-resident single-property ownership has generated over 10,000 legislative opinion submissions criticizing policy inconsistencies.
sections.International Economy: The Trump administration is pressuring allied nations to choose between U.S. and Chinese camps for AI and technology cooperation, with particular focus on Korea's semiconductor sector where China accounts for 45% of export share. The U.S. Federal Reserve held rates steady at 3.5-3.75% in July, but Bank of America predicts three successive 0.25 percentage point increases in September, October, and December. The upcoming FOMC minutes release on August 19 will be critical for assessing future interest rate trajectories and global financial market direction. Trade tensions and Section 301 investigation results expected by month-end create uncertainty for Korean exporters, while U.S. tariff threats against allied nations are undermining confidence in American economic leadership.
sections.AI & Economy: Artificial intelligence adoption is accelerating labor market disruptions, with salaried positions declining for four consecutive months for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly affecting youth employment in AI-intensive sectors like IT and professional services. Large enterprises are increasingly deploying AI agents with individual digital identities and access controls, with projections suggesting Fortune 500 companies will use over 150,000 AI agents by 2028 compared to fewer than 15 today. Despite semiconductor boom conditions, youth hiring has contracted sharply as firms reduce entry-level positions, creating a prolonged employment crisis that extends beyond traditional cyclical patterns. Self-employed business formation is surging as wage employment opportunities contract, indicating structural rather than temporary labor market deterioration.
sections.Others: SK Hynix's potential Solidigm IPO on NASDAQ is generating debate within securities markets regarding shareholder dilution versus strategic benefits of capital raising for the storage solution subsidiary. Leveraged single-stock ETF transactions have generated over 100 billion won in combined exchange and securities firm commissions during the two-month period before regulatory adjustments. Seoul Metropolitan Council's Democratic Party has proposed stabilizing Korea's TBS public broadcaster, which faces accumulated debt of 16.9 billion won and owes accumulated employee wages. Korea's trade negotiation chief position vacancy coincides with heightened U.S. pressure on investment commitment implementation and Section 301 tariff investigation outcomes expected by month-end, creating diplomatic coordination challenges.
